shelf.dragHint: Drag a record to file it where it really stands. A compartment you have arranged keeps the room you made in it; everything you have not placed keeps filling the compartments you left free.

shelf.filterHint: Clear the search and the format filter to rearrange the shelf by hand.
shelf.keptHint: The shelf stands as you left it: the records keep their places even when you add one or a copy leaves. A new record goes into whatever compartment is still free.

profile.your-account-and-how: Your account, and how the app behaves for you. What you set here is kept for the account, so it follows you to the next browser you sign in on.
profile.how-you-appear-in: How you appear in the app.

profile.the-theme-and-how: The theme and how much of the screen the pages use.
profile.demoTourIntro: The compass in the corner of the screen, which always shows the page you have open.
profile.what-the-collection-opens: What the collection opens with, and how much of an album page shows at once.
profile.the-furniture-your-records: The furniture your records stand in. Draw what you actually own — how many units, and how many compartments across and down — and the collection's shelf view is filed into it.
profile.how-the-player-starts: How the player starts, one setting per kind of page — a track page may well want a fuller stage than the rest.
profile.what-you-have-actually: What you have actually put on here, counted for the records rather than for an account somewhere else.
profile.what-other-collectors-get: What other collectors get to see about you. Nothing here is shared until you say so, and turning it back off takes it away at once.
profile.where-spotify-plays-and: Where Spotify plays, and how loud it starts here.
profile.sign-in-to-set: Sign in to set up your profile.

listSettings.albumCompact: Open album pages with the sections collapsed

profile.languageIntro: What the app speaks to you in. Kept with the account, so it follows you to the next browser you sign in on.
profile.genresIntro: Two genres at most. The app downloads the catalog of those genres only — your own collection stays whole either way.

track.synced-lyrics-lrc-for: Synced lyrics (LRC, for the lyrics player)
track.no-lyrics-here-lyrics: No lyrics here. Lyrics are shown only when you are signed in.

collection-item.this-copy-is-not: This copy is not in your collection.
collection-item.a-copy-page-only: A copy page only opens for the records you own — the shelf place, the price and the story on it are yours alone.
collection-item.sign-in-to-open: Sign in to open your copies.
collection-item.what-a-copy-page: What a copy page shows beyond the catalog belongs to the collector who owns it, so it needs to know who you are.
collection-item.nothing-is-written-down: Nothing is written down about this copy yet — when you got it, what you paid, how it has held up.

collection-item.no-tracklist-for-this: No tracklist for this album yet.

collections.sets-of-records-defined: Sets of records defined by a rule, not by a list — they grow with the catalog.
collections.no-collection-has-been: No challenge has been published yet. Once one is, this is where you see how far your shelf gets you.
collections.a-collection-pays-only: A challenge pays only once it is complete — these are the records that move that along fastest.
collections.star-the-collections-you: Star the challenges you are after — Following then keeps just those, however many are published.

daily-question.one-question-out-of: One question a day, the same for everybody, drawn out of the catalog. You get one guess, and then the answer.
daily-question.no-question-today: No question today. It is put together out of the catalog a few minutes after midnight; when there was not enough to build one, it tries again tomorrow.
daily-question.one-guess-only: One guess only — the answer shows the moment it is in.

failure.stale-day: The day turned while you were here — this is today’s question.
failure.no-question: There is no question for this day.
failure.signed-out: The session is gone. Sign in again and the guess can go.
failure.unknown: The guess did not get through. Try again.

daily-question.answered-late: The guess came after the time ran out: the answer is yours, the points are not.
daily-question.late-guess-is-free: Time is up — a guess no longer pays, but it still reveals the answer.

history.title: Past questions
history.played-of: You guessed on {{played}} of the last {{days}} days.
history.nothing-yet: No days behind you yet — today is the first question.

leaderboard.title: Leaderboard
leaderboard.rebuilt-nightly: The field is rebuilt once a day, in the evening; your points update at once, your place at the next run.

error.it-doesn-t-exist: It doesn't exist, or your account doesn't have access to it. Admin pages need an administrator login.

map.where-the-records-are: Where the records are kept. Everyone here chose to be on this map, and chose how much of themselves it shows —
map.your-own-is-in: your own is in the profile
map.sign-in-to-see: Sign in to see where the other collectors are.
map.nobody-shares-where-they: Nobody shares where they are yet. You could be the first.
map.drag-to-move-scroll: Drag to move, scroll to zoom, and pick a pin to see who is there.
map.no-one-on-the: No one on the map yet.

musician.this-musician-is-not: This musician is not in the catalog.

network.no-connections-to-show: No connections to show. Pick another focus or change the filters.
network.the-network-is-too: The network is too large to show in full — lower the depth or hide guests.

radio.a-record-chosen-for: A record chosen for you: what the catalog has just taken in, what your shelf says you like, one compartment of that shelf, a challenge you are after — or nothing in particular.
radio.draw-the-records-out: Draw the records out of a hat instead of playing the station as it comes.
radio.nothing-to-play-yet: Nothing to play yet. The radio needs records with a Spotify or YouTube link behind them — add a few to the catalog and the stations appear here.

blocked.signIn: The radio plays records through YouTube and Spotify. Sign in to listen — both are somebody else's player, and neither is put on the page for a visitor.
blocked.consentBefore: The radio plays records through YouTube and Spotify. Embedding either one writes its owner's storage and tells them you were here, so it takes your leave first — the bar at the bottom asks, and the
blocked.consentAfter: takes the answer back at any time.

release.the-catalog-holds-the: The catalog holds the album it belonged to, but this edition of it is not in it — or no longer is.
release.this-is-the-only: This is the only pressing of the album the catalog knows.

scan.photograph-the-sleeve-the: Photograph the sleeve — the back cover with the barcode or the catalogue number works best.
scan.your-account-may-not: Your account may not add records to a collection yet. Ask for the collector role and the scan opens up.
scan.sign-in-as-a: Sign in as a collector to add records to your collection.
scan.nothing-recognised-on-this: Nothing recognised on this photo. Try the back cover, with the barcode or the catalogue number in frame.
scan.title: Title
scan.label: Label

shelf-scan.photograph-one-compartment-twice: Photograph one compartment from two angles. Reading it twice is what tells you which spines the app got right and which need your eyes.
shelf-scan.your-account-may-not: Your account may not add records to a collection yet. Ask for the collector role and the scan opens up.
shelf-scan.sign-in-as-a: Sign in as a collector to add records to your collection.
shelf-scan.one-from-the-front: One straight on, one from the side. The glare that hides a black spine moves with the angle.
shelf-scan.no-spine-could-be: No spine could be read. Try a closer photo, or more light from the side.
shelf-scan.the-photos-counted-differently: The photos counted a different number of records ({{counts}}). One of them saw a spine that is not in this list.
shelf-scan.label: Label
shelf-scan.nothing-could-be-read: Nothing could be read off this spine — fill it in or leave it out.
shelf-scan.an-admin-approves-each: An admin approves each request; nothing enters the catalogue before that.

upcoming.the-next-few-weeks: The next few weeks of records by the artists already in the catalog — new ones and reissues alike, gathered from MusicBrainz once a day.
upcoming.nothing-is-announced-for: Nothing is announced for the coming weeks. Once a record by one of the catalog's artists gets a date on MusicBrainz, it shows up here — usually a few weeks ahead.
upcoming.matched-on-the-artist: Matched on the artist's name only — it could be a namesake.

filteredOut.one: Nothing in the next few weeks matches that. There is still {{count}} record coming.
filteredOut.other: Nothing in the next few weeks matches that. There are still {{count}} records coming.

wishlist-item.either-the-record-has: Either the record has been found and the wish struck off, or it was never on anyone's list.
wishlist-item.this-wish-is-no: This wish is no longer active — the record was found, or the hunt was called off.
wishlist-item.the-catalog-knows-no: The catalog knows no pressing of this album yet.

owned-artist.title: My bands
owned-artist.lead: When the catalog has never heard of a band, you can enter it here. Only you see it, and it counts towards no score and no statistic.
owned-artist.could-not-save: It could not be saved. Try again.
owned-artist.nothing-yet: You have no bands of your own yet.
owned-artist.only-yours: What you enter here stays yours — only an approval takes it into the catalog.
owned-artist.could-not-submit: It could not be submitted. Try again.

propose.lead: Change what you think the catalog has wrong. Saving writes nothing — the next step asks what backs it, and then it goes to an admin.
propose.every-field-needs-one: Every changed field needs something behind it: a link, a catalogue number, or your own words if the record is in your hands.
propose.reference-placeholder: A link, an id, or a sentence
propose.anything-else: Anything else the admin should know (optional)
propose.sent: Sent. An admin decides field by field, and gives a reason for anything they turn down.
propose.nothing-to-send: You have nothing to send. Open an artist and suggest a change there.
propose.could-not-send: It could not be sent. Try again.
propose.say-where-it-is-from: Say how you know if you can — a link, a catalogue number, or that the record is in your hands. It can be sent either way.

my-request.title: My requests
my-request.lead: What you asked the catalog to take in, and what came back. A refusal carries its reason — that is what you can answer.
my-request.could-not-read: Your requests could not be read.
my-request.nothing-yet: You have not sent anything yet.
my-request.missing-something: Is something missing from the catalog?

recordShelf.no-drawn-compartment-left: No drawn compartment is left, or none is tall enough for these — look over your shelving in your profile.

copyPhotos.at-most-two-pictures: At most two pictures — the front and the back. They are scaled down in the browser before anything is uploaded.

copyRemoval.it-stays-in-your: It stays in your history, and you can take it back any time.
copyRemoval.numberTakenMeanwhile: The copy is back, but its number has been registered by another collector in the meantime.

releasePicker.which-one-of-them: Which one of them is yours? An edition size on its own says nothing about this copy.

releasePicker.discogs-lists-no-pressings: Discogs lists no pressings of it.
releasePicker.photograph-the-record-the: Photograph the record — the back cover or the label, so the catalogue number or the barcode is legible. That is what tells your pressing from the others.
releasePicker.or-paste-an-image: or paste an image, or drop one here
releasePicker.nothing-recognised-on-this: Nothing recognised on this photo. Try the side with the catalogue number or the barcode.

releasePicker.photo-route-hint: Photograph the back cover or the label, and we look up which pressing it is.
releasePicker.describe-route-hint: Paste its Discogs link, or describe it in a few words.
releasePicker.paste-not-an-image: That was not an image. Copy the picture itself — in a browser, right-click it and choose “Copy image”. A file copied from Finder cannot be pasted, but you can drop it here.

visualLab.minden-csal-dhoz-egy: One record per family, so every world of the engine can be stepped through.

playerStage.no-synced-lyrics-saved: No synced lyrics saved for this track: the text scrolls with the song.

joinPrompt.pitch: The catalog is open to everyone — {{albums}} albums of {{artists}} artists to read through. Sign in to keep the copies you own, see what a challenge is still missing and have your shelf follow you between devices.

badgeSettings.a-collection-s-badge: A collection's badge is drawn once by an image model, from the collection's own data, and then it is fixed.
badgeSettings.switched-off-no-badge: Switched off, no badge can be drawn and nothing can be spent.
badgeSettings.the-vertex-region-not: The Vertex region — not necessarily the one the database is in.
badgeSettings.how-many-the-admin: How many the admin picks between. More costs more, and every one of them is billed.
badgeSettings.the-ceiling-for-the: The ceiling for the whole day, counted on the server. A loop that goes wrong stops here instead of on the invoice.
badgeSettings.the-style-lock-the: The style lock — the fixed sentences every badge is drawn from — and the style version live in code. They are the only reason a shelf of badges reads as one set: if a curator could edit them per badge, the set would drift apart within weeks. Changing them is a deliberate act, and it means regenerating every badge.

releaseRequestRow.not-in-the-catalog: Not in the catalog — approving creates the album too
releaseRequestRow.add-the-release-to: Add the release to the album in the admin, then link it here.

releaseRequestAdmin.error-not-found: Not found: the request, its album, the release or the Discogs release.
releaseRequestAdmin.error-moved-on: Already decided — or it has no Discogs release: link a catalog release.
releaseRequestAdmin.error-not-allowed: Only an admin may decide requests.
releaseRequestAdmin.error-discogs-unreachable: Discogs cannot be reached right now. Try again later.
releaseRequestAdmin.error-discogs-busy: Discogs is busy right now. Try again in a minute.
releaseRequestAdmin.error-unknown: Something went wrong. Try again later.

musicCollectionAdmin.sets-of-records-defined: Sets of records defined by a rule. What belongs to one is resolved against the catalog, so a collection grows with it — and the badge is earned by owning all of them.
musicCollectionAdmin.whoever-earned-its-badge: ? Whoever earned its badge loses it, and this cannot be undone here.

musicCollectionEdit.a-collection-is-a: A collection is a rule, not a list: what belongs to it is resolved against the catalog every time it is read.
musicCollectionEdit.name: Name
musicCollectionEdit.a-primeicons-class-as: A PrimeIcons class, as in the menu.
musicCollectionEdit.a-draft-is-not: A draft is not listed and earns nobody a badge.
musicCollectionEdit.every-filter-given-must: Every filter given must hold. A filter left empty says nothing — with all of them empty the collection asks for the whole catalog.
musicCollectionEdit.discogs-roles-comma-separated: Discogs roles, comma separated. One credit must satisfy both: the musician in that role, not two credits together.
musicCollectionEdit.without-a-name-the: Without a name the collection rewards no badge.
musicCollectionEdit.a-hand-made-image: A hand-made image, for the rare badge that wants one. The generated pin below wins over it.
musicCollectionEdit.drawn-by-an-image: Drawn by an image model, from this collection's own data. The style is the same on every badge — only the motif, the enamel, the patina and the rim follow the rule. Every image drawn is kept, so the pin can be any of them, today or next year.
musicCollectionEdit.save-the-collection-first: Save the collection first: the prompt is built on the server from what is stored, not from this form.
musicCollectionEdit.no-filter-yet-this: No filter yet — this rule takes in the whole catalog. Publishing it is refused.
musicCollectionEdit.points-and-only-once: points, and only once a collector owns every one of them. Owning the original pressing of an old record raises it further.

pointsHint.one: What finishing it is worth. Left empty the rule decides — how many records it asks for, and how old they are — which right now would be {{count}} point.
pointsHint.other: What finishing it is worth. Left empty the rule decides — how many records it asks for, and how old they are — which right now would be {{count}} points.

profilePrivacy.puts-youtube-s-and: Puts YouTube's and Spotify's players on the page. They are not ours: each one writes its own storage and tells its owner you were here. Switching it off takes them off the page at once, and the records go silent.
profilePrivacy.count-how-the-app: Count how the app is used
profilePrivacy.which-pages-and-features: Which pages and features get opened, through Google Analytics. No advertising, and nothing about your records or your searches. Switching it off stops it at once and clears what it left in this browser.

profilePlayback.show-the-lyrics-when: Show the lyrics when there are any
profilePlayback.play-on-to-the: Play on to the next track

profileShelves.draw-the-shelving-you: Draw the shelving you actually own. A unit is a grid of compartments, and a compartment has two measurements: its height decides what fits (an LP needs 32 cm, a DVD 20, a CD 12, a cassette 8) and its length decides how much. Records are filed from the first unit to the last — and whatever a compartment cannot take waits for the next one.
profileShelves.nothing-drawn-yet-the: Nothing drawn yet — the collection stands on one open wall that grows with it.

short.one: {{count}} record has nowhere to stand — it shows below the furniture until you draw more.
short.other: {{count}} records have nowhere to stand — they show below the furniture until you draw more.

profileShelves.roomNote: {{units}} units · {{compartments}} compartments · {{length}} cm of shelf in all, which takes {{holds}} of your records.
profileShelves.how-the-copies-lie: How the copies lie in a compartment
profileShelves.nothing-fits: Nothing fits a compartment this low

profileSpotify.your-own-app-explained: With your own Spotify app this player drives Spotify: the queue, the radio, the next track, your own speakers. Without it, Spotify's embedded frame on the album page is what is left — it plays in full if you are signed in to Spotify, but nothing here drives it. Spotify counts who signs in through an app — one app holds twenty-five people — which is why yours has to be your own.
profileSpotify.step-create-app: Open developer.spotify.com/dashboard and create an app (Web Playback SDK).
profileSpotify.step-redirect-uri: Add this to the app's Redirect URIs:
profileSpotify.step-copy-client-id: Copy the app's Client ID here.
profileSpotify.same-account-and-premium: Create the app with the same Spotify account you will sign in with: an app in development mode lets nobody in but its own owner. Playback driven from here also needs Spotify Premium — without it the player does not start at all.
profileSpotify.client-id-placeholder: The 32-character id from your app's page
profileSpotify.speakers-show-up-when: Speakers show up when they support Spotify Connect and are on. Missing? Play something on it once from the Spotify app, then refresh.
profileSpotify.what-the-browser-player: What the browser player starts at. This one stays in the browser rather than the account — the speakers differ from machine to machine.

profileAppearance.the-wide-setting-only: The wide setting only shows on a screen with room to spare.

profileDemoTour.puts-the-play-button: Puts a compass in the corner of every page, and lets the tour be started from here as well.

profileListening.nothing-yet-put-a: Nothing yet. Put a record on from an album page and it is counted here — a record counts once it has played for half a minute, and counts as heard right through once every track of it has been.

profileAccount.note: This is the name shown next to what you add to the catalog.

nextAlbums.the-moment-it-is: the moment it is on the shelf

consentBar.may-we-count-which: May we count which pages and features get used? Google Analytics, no advertising — what you own and what you search for stays out of it.
consentBar.may-we-put-youtube: May we put YouTube's and Spotify's players on the page so you can listen here? They are not ours: each one writes its own storage and tells its owner you were here. Without this the records stay silent.
consentBar.you-can-change-either: You can change either of these any time on your profile.

playerPanel.this-player-only-plays: This is Spotify's own frame: it plays in full if you are signed in to Spotify, but nothing here drives it. Connect your Spotify Premium account (play button or settings) for the queue, the radio and your own speakers.
playerPanel.spotifys-own-frame: This is Spotify's own frame: the play button above starts it, and it plays in full if you are signed in to Spotify. For the queue, the radio and your own speakers, name your own Spotify app in your profile.

playerSettingsMenu.speakers-show-up-when: Speakers show up when they support Spotify Connect and are on. Missing? Play something on it once from the Spotify app, then refresh.
playerSettingsMenu.play-on-to-the: Play on to the next track
playerSettingsMenu.stop-to-turn-the: Stop to turn the record over
playerSettingsMenu.own-app-in-profile: To drive Spotify from here — queue, radio, speakers — name your own Spotify app in your profile.

form.savingKeepsBoth: Saving keeps both — merge one away in the catalog.

profileLanguage.chosen: Your own pick. The app's default no longer applies to you.
profileLanguage.following: Following the app's default, or what your browser asks for.

artistMembers.heading: Members ({{count}})
artistMembers.musician-fixed: The band and the musician are what identify this row; remove it and add another one to change the musician.
artistMembers.instruments-hint: Pick what they play; each language reads the list in its own words.
artistMembers.to-hint: Leave it empty when the end year is unknown.
artistMembers.delete-question: Remove {{name}} from the line-up? The musician stays in the catalog.
artistMembers.no-members-yet: No members yet. Add them by hand, or let the Discogs import fill the line-up in.
artistMembers.error-duplicate: This musician is already in the line-up. Edit that row instead.
artistMembers.error-permission: You may not change the line-up.
artistMembers.error-general: Something went wrong. Try again later.
artistMembers.load-hint: Load the line-up from MusicBrainz and the catalog’s own credits
artistMembers.pick-the-band: Pick the band whose line-up this is — save its id on the Details tab to make the choice stick.
artistMembers.found-note: Members and years from MusicBrainz, guests and instruments from the credits already in the catalog. Musicians already in the line-up are left out.
artistMembers.adding: Adding the rows… new musicians are created one at a time, which can take a few seconds.
artistMembers.error-nothing-found: Nothing to add: no line-up on MusicBrainz, and the catalog has no credits for this band’s albums.
artistMembers.external-failed: MusicBrainz could not be reached, so only the catalog’s own credits are listed. Try the load again later for the members and their years.
artistMembers.instruments-empty: No such instrument on the list.

musicianBands.heading: Bands ({{count}})
musicianBands.no-bands-yet: This musician is not in any line-up yet.
musicianBands.edit-on-the-band: Edit a line-up on the band’s own page, under Line-up.
musicianBands.error-general: Something went wrong. Try again later.

dailyQuestionBanner.there-is-a-question: Today's question is up, and you have not guessed yet.

dailyQuestionSettings.title: Daily question
dailyQuestionSettings.lead: The rules of the game: how long there is to answer, what a guess pays, and what the engine may ask about.
dailyQuestionSettings.switched-off: Switched off, no new question is composed and the page says so. The days already composed stay as they are.
dailyQuestionSettings.time-limit-hint: How long there is to answer. Zero takes the clock off, and with it the speed bonus. A late guess is still taken — it just pays nothing.
dailyQuestionSettings.streak-bonus-hint: The first day of a run pays no bonus: the bonus is for coming back.
dailyQuestionSettings.speed-bonus-hint: Paid on a sliding scale: all of it for an instant answer, nothing for one that used up the clock. Without a clock it pays nothing.
dailyQuestionSettings.bonus-day-chance-hint: Drawn from the day itself, so the same day is a bonus day for everybody.
dailyQuestionSettings.question-kinds-hint: What you switch off is never drawn. The material-hungry kinds switch themselves on as the data fills in — switching one off always wins.
dailyQuestionSettings.leaderboard-size-hint: Everybody else still sees their own place: the nightly run writes it into their pot.
dailyQuestionSettings.compose-exists: {{day}}: the question was already up; nothing was overwritten.
dailyQuestionSettings.compose-disabled: The game is switched off, so no question was composed.
dailyQuestionSettings.compose-no-material: There was not enough in the catalog to make a question.
dailyQuestionSettings.history-hint: What the game has been asking. The answers are not in the list — those stay on the server. The composing looks a fortnight back: it will not ask about the same album again until then, about the same kind of question for a week, or about the same artist for four days.

requestAdmin.what-collectors-ask: Everything the collectors ask of the catalog, in one place: what they want it to take in, and the pressings they ask for. A catalog request is decided field by field — a refusal needs a reason, and the collector reads it.
requestAdmin.error-not-found: The request, or the catalog document it is about, is gone.
requestAdmin.error-moved-on: The catalog has changed since, or the request was already decided. Reload the page.
requestAdmin.error-invalid: The decision is incomplete: every field needs a verdict, and every refusal a reason.
requestAdmin.error-not-allowed: Only an admin may decide requests.
requestAdmin.error-unknown: Something went wrong. Try again later.

requestRow.decide-every-field: Every field needs a verdict, and every refusal a reason.

profileAvatar.yours: This is your character. It appears in the top bar, on the map, and wherever you stand next to other collectors.
profileAvatar.none: You have no character yet. Build one and it becomes your picture, in place of a photo.
profileAvatar.note: What you build is kept with your account, and you can come back and change it.

avatarFigure.unavailable: This piece has not been drawn yet — the character stays as it was.

needs.patch: A patch is sewn onto a vest or jacket — a t-shirt has no back for one.
needs.tattoo: The ink shows on a bare arm; a jacket sleeve covers it.

profileGenres.following: Browsing, search and the radio stay inside the genres you follow.
profileGenres.everything: The whole catalog is downloaded, every genre of it.
profileGenres.rebuild: The app rebuilds its local catalog and reloads the page.

genre.title: Genres and styles
genre.intro: The genres and the styles under them. Both catalog forms choose from this list, and an online load matches what the sources name against it.
genre.name: Name
genre.name-taken: A genre of this name already exists.
genre.in-use: An artist in the catalog carries this genre, so it cannot be deleted. Retire it instead: it leaves the forms, and the styles already saved keep their genre.
genre.empty: No genre yet. Add the first one — the forms choose from this list.
genre.style-hint: Type a style and press Enter. A comma takes several at once.

visibility.link: Link — readable by whoever knows it

summary.noRule: No rule — matches the whole catalog

language.title: Default language
language.intro: The language the app opens in for a reader who has not picked one. Anybody who has chosen keeps their choice — including you.
language.heading: Which language
language.hint: A visitor whose browser asks for a language the app does not speak sees this one.
language.unset: Nothing is set: the app follows each browser, and falls back to English.

role.title: Roles
role.intro: A role is the only place a permission is granted. What you tick here the server adds up for every user who holds the role — one save changes what a group of people may do.
role.name: Name
role.id-hint: Id: {{id}} — fixed once the role is created.
role.id-kept: Id: {{id}} — it stays even if the role is renamed.
role.wildcard-hint: Passes every check, whatever else is ticked.

group.catalog-hint: The shared catalog: artists, albums, releases and what hangs off them.
group.collector-hint: A collector's own copies and wishlist.
group.owned-hint: What a collector adds for themselves when the catalog does not know it yet.
group.access-hint: Roles, users, and reading the effective permissions.
group.pages-hint: Access to one admin page at a time. Full access gets in without them.

role.baseline-hint: The USER role carries it, and the server puts that role on every user the moment their document appears. It is not handed out here: this is what it takes to put a record on one's own shelf. A role adds to it.
role.extra-hint: The role carries permissions this page does not know — written by a script, or left from a resource since renamed. They are kept on save.
role.empty: No role yet. Add the first one — without it nobody has a single permission.
role.in-use: {{count}} user(s) hold this role, so it cannot be deleted. Take it off them first, or empty its permissions.
role.copy-of: A copy of {{name}} — the permissions came along; the name is yours to give.
role.reaches-nobody: Nobody holds this role at the moment.
role.reaches-unknown: Cannot tell how many users it reaches — that needs permission to list the users.
role.reaches-new: A new role: nobody holds it until it is given.
role.holders-unreadable: Cannot tell who holds the role, so it cannot be deleted. That needs permission to list the users (viewUserEntity).

finding.name-too-long: The name may be at most {{max}} characters.
finding.name-taken: A role by that name already exists. The permission sync matches on the name as well, so it could not tell the two apart.
finding.id-taken: That name would take the id {{id}}, which is already in use. Pick another name.
finding.locks-me-out: This save would take away your own way back into these pages. Grant it to another of your roles first.
finding.no-permissions: This role grants nothing. That is fine if it is meant — it is how a role is emptied instead of deleted.
finding.wildcard-redundant: Next to full access the other {{count}} tick(s) count for nothing. If that is the intent, they can come off.
finding.edit-page-without-write: {{resource}}: the editor opens, but the rules will refuse the save — the create or update permission is missing.
finding.user-admin-without-view: Users may be written but not listed: the user page opens on nobody. Add the view permission too.
finding.role-delete-without-user-view: Roles may be deleted, but who holds one cannot be established — so the delete cannot run. Add the view permission on users.

write-failed.name-taken: Somebody created a role by that name in the meantime.
write-failed.id-taken: Somebody took that id in the meantime.

user.title: Users and roles
user.intro: Who holds which role. A permission comes from a role — all that is decided here is who gets it. The effective permissions are worked out by the server; the eye shows what it came to.
user.search: Search by name, email or id
user.dangling: Points at a role that does not exist: {{names}}
user.no-effective: The server has not worked out permissions for this user yet.
user.would-lock-out: You cannot take away your own way back into these pages.

bandOfTheWeek.name: Band of the week: {{name}}
bandOfTheWeek.description: Every fourth record is theirs, your taste and the catalog in between.

justIn.description: The records the catalog has taken in most recently.
justIn.name: Just in

yourTaste.description: Records in the styles your shelf is fullest of — owned or not.
yourTaste.name: Your taste

yourShelf.description: Your own copies, one after another.
yourShelf.name: Your shelf

anything.description: The catalog, in no order whatsoever.
anything.name: Anything at all

unit.description: The records you filed into this unit, read out the way they stand.

collection.description: Every record this challenge asks for.

search.title: Find a record
search.content: One field for the whole catalog: an artist, an album or a track, and the results come while you type.

spotlight.title: One act in the light
spotlight.content: The home page always puts one artist forward: the band of the week, or — on a week nobody was chosen for — a draw from the catalog. Shuffle it if you would rather see somebody else.

catalog.title: What the catalog holds
catalog.content: Artists, albums, pressings and tracks, and how much of all that already has a cover, a year and a label on it.

coverage.title: How much of it is collected
coverage.content: The catalog's albums by decade, and how many of them are already on a shelf — signed in, it is your own collection drawn onto it.

artists.title: The acts
artists.content: The artist pages open from here: their records, who played in them, and who those musicians played with elsewhere.

styles.title: By style
styles.content: The catalog broken up by genre: a row of albums for each style, to read on from.

decades.title: By decade
decades.content: The same by age: how many records the catalog holds from each decade, either side of the eighties.

acts.title: Bands, projects and formations
acts.content: Not every act is a band: the catalog keeps solo projects, supergroups and one-off formations apart.

albums.title: The newest albums
albums.content: What went into the catalog last — by when it was written down, not by when it came out.

guest.name: The home page
guest.description: A minute on the home page: what the catalog holds, and what it becomes once you sign in.

welcome.title: Welcome
welcome.content: This is musiCollection: a catalog of records — artists, albums, pressings. Here is the home page in a minute.

bar.title: The bar
bar.content: Everything starts here: the pages a visitor may browse, and to the right the language and the light or dark theme.

recent.title: What arrived lately
recent.content: The catalog's latest entries: what collectors have most recently written down in it.

challenges.title: Challenges
challenges.content: Sets of records a rule defines: a label's series, a decade, a band's whole output. Signed in, you also see how far you have got in each.

join.title: What signing in adds
join.content: A shelf of your own, a wishlist, radio made of your own records, challenges and the question of the day — all of it hangs on an account.

login.title: This is the way in
login.content: One click with a Google account. The tour changes with it: the next one shows you what is yours.

collector.name: Your home page
collector.description: A minute on the home page: what it brings out of the catalog, and what it brings off your own shelf.

welcome.title: Welcome back
welcome.content: This is your home page: the catalog at the top, and below it the rows that come off your own shelf. A minute, and we have been through it.

bar.title: The bar
bar.content: Everything starts here. On a wide screen the pages sit in a row, on a phone they are behind the menu button, and the language and the theme are always to the right.

recent.title: What arrived lately
recent.content: The copies you put on the shelf most recently — or, on a week you added none, what the catalog itself has gained.

challenges.title: Challenges
challenges.content: Sets of records a rule defines: a label's series, a decade, a band's whole output. The bar shows how far you are, and the page suggests which record would pay the most.

hunt.title: The next record
hunt.content: What would be worth buying next: the records missing from the challenges you are closest to finishing, in order.

account.title: And the rest is here
account.content: Your shelf, the scan, the radio, the wishlist and the profile — and in the profile this tour can be switched off once you have seen it.

intro.title: Your own shelf
intro.content: From here on it is yours: how many records you have, from how many artists, in what format. Nobody else sees this page.

stats.title: At a glance
stats.content: How many records, from how many artists, in what format — and what the shelf is worth, where you wrote down what you paid.

views.title: Three ways to look
views.content: A wall of covers, a plain list, or the shelf itself, with every copy where it really stands. The furniture is drawn in the profile.

decades.title: By decade
decades.content: Your own records laid out by age: it shows at once which decade you collect hardest.

styles.title: By style
styles.content: The same thing by genre: how much punk, how much jazz, how much of everything else stands on your shelf.

challenges.title: Your challenges
challenges.content: The ones you have started, and how much of each your shelf already holds. The full list opens from here.

search.title: Search your own
search.content: Searches your records only — by artist and by album title, as you type.

formats.title: By format
formats.content: Keep only the vinyl, the CDs or the tapes. The number on the chip says how many there are.

sort.title: Sorting and grouping
sort.content: Order by artist, by year or by the day you got it — and group them the way you think of them.

shelf.title: The shelf as it stands
shelf.content: The shelf view draws every copy where it actually stands. You lay the furniture out in the profile.

intro.title: A record from a photograph
intro.content: Photograph the sleeve. The catalog reads the cover, says which record it thinks it is, and the copy is on your shelf a few taps later.

shot.title: The photograph
shot.content: This is where it starts: take a picture of the sleeve, or pick one from the gallery. Keep the cover in frame, as square as you can.

results.title: What it thinks it is
results.content: What the catalog turned up from the photograph, the likeliest first. Pick the one that is yours.

read.title: What it read off the picture
read.content: The text it found on the sleeve — that is what it searched with. If it misread, this is where you see why.

intro.title: A whole compartment at once
intro.content: One photograph of a row of spines, and every record it can make out is offered together — this is how a shelf that is already full gets in.

shots.title: The photographs
shots.content: Several at a time: work along the compartment spine by spine, picture after picture.

controls.title: What is in the compartment
controls.content: Say whether it is vinyl, CD or tape — that narrows what it looks for — then set it reading.

review.title: Going through them
review.content: Every spine it recognised, one by one: accept it, correct it, or skip it. Only what you approve reaches your shelf.

intro.title: What is still missing
intro.content: The records you are after, with what you would pay for them. The hunt list on the home page is built out of this.

stats.title: Where you stand
stats.content: How many records you are hunting, from how many artists — and how many you have already found.

search.title: Search
search.content: Searches inside the wishlist, by artist and by title.

formats.title: By format
formats.content: If you only want it on vinyl, narrow the list down to it.

found.title: The ones you found
found.content: What you have already got is out of the way by default. This switch brings it back.

gotIt.title: Got it
gotIt.content: Once you have it, one tap moves it to your shelf and takes it off the list.

intro.title: Challenges
intro.content: Sets of records a rule defines, not a list — a label's series, a decade, a band's whole output. Finish one and it pays.

stats.title: The figures
stats.content: How many challenges there are, how many you have started, and how many you have finished.

hunt.title: The next record
hunt.content: What would be worth buying most: the records missing from your nearly finished challenges, in order.

tabs.title: Filtering
tabs.content: All of them, the ones you started, the ones you follow, or the ones already done.

card.title: One challenge
card.content: The artwork, the rule, and how many records it asks for. Tap it and the full list opens.

progress.title: Where you stand
progress.content: The bar counts your own shelf against the records the challenge asks for.

follow.title: Following
follow.content: Follow it and you can keep an eye on what is missing from the home page too.

intro.title: Your own radio
intro.content: A record drawn off your shelf and put on, side after side. In order or shuffled, and what actually played is kept in the log.

order.title: In order or shuffled
order.content: Turn it on and the radio draws your records out at random.

onAir.title: What is playing
onAir.content: The broadcast as it runs: the record, the side, and how far in it is. This is where you stop it.

stations.title: The stations
stations.content: Each station picks off your shelf differently: by genre, by decade, or by what has not been played for a long time. Choose one and it starts.

intro.title: The question of the day
intro.content: One question out of the catalog, the same for everybody, once a day. Points, a streak to keep alive, and a leaderboard.

history.title: The questions before
history.content: Everything asked so far, with your answers to it — and which ones you got right.

score.title: Where you stand
score.content: Points, streak, longest streak and hit rate. A single missed day breaks the streak.

question.title: Today’s question
question.content: The same one for everybody, out of the catalog. One a day, and you answer once.

clock.title: The clock
clock.content: While it runs, a right answer is worth more. No need to rush — but no need to brood either.

options.title: The answers
options.content: A few to choose from, one of them right. The moment you choose, you see which it was.

leaderboard.title: The leaderboard
leaderboard.content: How you stand against everybody else. Only those who have played are on it.

intro.title: Coming out
intro.content: What the artists in the catalog are putting out next, gathered once a day — so a reissue you want does not slip past you.

stats.title: The figures
stats.content: How many releases are ahead, and how many of them come from the catalog’s own artists.

tabs.title: Filtering
tabs.content: All of them, or only the artists you collect.

timeline.title: The timeline
timeline.content: Month by month, day by day, what comes out when. Gathered once a day.

intro.title: Collectors
intro.content: Where the records are kept. Your own pin is only ever as precise as you allowed in the profile.

stats.title: The figures
stats.content: How many collectors and how many countries reached the map — as much as they chose to share.

world.title: The map
world.content: Drag it, scroll it, tap a pin. Your own shows exactly as much as you allowed in the profile.

countries.title: The countries
countries.content: Where the collectors are, country by country. Tap one and only those stay.

collectors.title: The collectors there
collectors.content: Everybody from that country who chose to say they are there.

intro.title: Give something back
intro.content: An artist, an album or a pressing the catalog does not know yet? Propose it here, and follow what became of what you sent.

propose.title: Propose something
propose.content: Missing an artist, an album, a pressing or a label? The form starts here, and what you send comes back to this page.

list.title: What you sent in
list.content: Every proposal of yours, and what became of it: waiting, taken, or handed back with a reason.

intro.title: Your profile
intro.content: Your account, and everything that fits the app to you: the language, the theme, the drawing of your shelf, playback, and what you share with others.

tabs.title: Four groups
tabs.content: The settings on four tabs: your account, your collecting, playback, and your data. One tab shows at a time — the tour opens all four in turn, and puts the page back where it found it.

accountTab.title: First tab: your account
accountTab.content: We start here. This tab is what the app knows about you: your name, the language, the look — and the switch for this tour. Move on and I will open it.

account.title: Your account
account.content: Your name as the catalog shows it, and the account you signed in with.

avatar.title: Your avatar
avatar.content: No photo? Build a character instead — build, face, hair, clothes — and it stands wherever a profile picture would.

language.title: The language
language.content: Hungarian, English or German. It stays with the account, so it follows you to the next browser.

appearance.title: The look
appearance.content: Dark or light, and how much of the screen’s width the pages are allowed to use.

collectionTab.title: Second tab: collecting
collectionTab.content: This tab is about your records: what the collection opens on, and the shelves they stand in. Move on and I will open it.

genres.title: Your genres
genres.content: Two genres at most, and the app downloads the catalog of those alone. It decides what browsing, search and the radio have to work with.

lists.title: The lists
lists.content: What the collection opens on, and how it orders your records.

shelves.title: Your shelves
shelves.content: The furniture your records stand in: how many compartments, and how big. The shelf view is drawn from this.

playbackTab.title: Third tab: playback
playbackTab.content: This tab is about sound: which player is allowed to play, and your Spotify account. Move on and I will open it.

playback.title: Playback
playback.content: Which player is allowed to sound, and what you let onto the page.

spotify.title: Spotify
spotify.content: Connect the account and your records play through your own Spotify.

dataTab.title: Fourth tab: your data
dataTab.content: The last tab is about what gets written down and what leaves you: your listening log, and what other collectors see of you. Move on and I will open it.

listening.title: The listening log
listening.content: What is written down about what actually played at your place.

privacy.title: Your data
privacy.content: What others see of you: your place on the map, your name on the leaderboard. Nothing, until you say so.

back.title: Back to the first
back.content: That is all four tabs. I am taking you back to the account tab, where I found you — one thing is left.

switch.title: And here is the switch
switch.content: The compass sits in the corner of every page, and it always shows the page you have open. Switch it off and it is gone; switch it back on when you want it again.

intro.title: The network
intro.content: Who played with whom: the catalog's musicians and bands in one graph, where shared members are what tie the bands together.

focus.title: The centre
focus.content: This is where you choose what stands at the middle of the graph, and how far from it to look.

search.title: Search the network
search.content: Type a band’s or a musician’s name and the graph jumps to them.

graph.title: The graph
graph.content: The dots are bands and musicians, the lines are shared membership. Drag it, scroll it, tap a dot.

legend.title: The key
legend.content: What each colour means, and what each line ties together.

details.title: What you picked
details.content: Whatever you tapped: who its members are, where the network ties it, and where to go on.

intro.title: One record, as you have it
intro.content: Not the album in general, but this one copy: how you bought it, how it looks, where it stands.

photos.title: Your own photographs
photos.content: Photograph the sleeve, the record, the inserts. These pictures stay yours; they are not the catalog’s.

facts.title: What this copy is
facts.content: Price, condition, where and when you got it, where it stands on the shelf. Edit rewrites any of it.

form.title: The form
form.content: What you write here belongs to your copy alone — it never overwrites what the catalog holds for everybody.

intro.title: What you are hunting
intro.content: The record as the catalog knows it — and what you added: what you would pay, and which pressing it has to be.

facts.title: What the record is
facts.content: Label, year, format, catalog number — enough to know it when it turns up in a shop.

intro.title: Your bands
intro.content: The artists you were given the keys to: this is where you edit your own bands’ pages.

list.title: What you look after
list.content: Every band that is yours. Editing opens from here, and so does handing it back.

intro.title: The challenge
intro.content: The rule that holds these records together, and what finishing it takes.

progress.title: Where you stand
progress.content: This much of the challenge’s records is already on your own shelf.

score.title: What it pays
score.content: A base score for every record you have, and a bonus for bringing the whole run together.

badge.title: The badge
badge.content: Finish it and this badge goes beside your name.

filter.title: Filtering
filter.content: Show all of them, or only what is still missing from your shelf.

grid.title: The records
grid.content: The challenge in full. What you have is marked; the rest is what there is to hunt.

intro.title: The artist
intro.content: The band’s or the solo artist’s page: where they came from, when they formed, what they play.

stats.title: The figures
stats.content: How many albums the catalog has of theirs, how many of those are yours, and how far their run reaches.

nav.title: The parts of the page
nav.content: Jump to a section: the biography, the line-up, the records, the artists like them.

about.title: The biography
about.content: What the catalog knows about them. If it is thin, the proposal button is how you fill it in.

lineup.title: The line-up
lineup.content: Who played in the band, and from when to when. Each musician’s own page opens from here.

discography.title: The records
discography.content: Every album in the catalog, by year. What you have is marked.

collection.title: What you have of theirs
collection.content: Your own copies from this artist, pressing by pressing.

similar.title: Alike
similar.content: Artists in the same genre, or ones that worked with the same musicians.

intro.title: The album
intro.content: The album as the catalog knows it: the artist, the year, the genre and the sleeve.

collect.title: Put it on the shelf
collect.content: One tap and your copy joins the collection — you can name the pressing while you are at it.

wish.title: Onto the wishlist
wish.content: If you do not have it yet, this is how it joins what you are hunting.

challenges.title: In challenges
challenges.content: Which challenges this record belongs to, and what getting it would bring in.

original.title: The first pressing
original.content: The original release: when it came out, on which label, in which format.

listen.title: Listen to it
listen.content: If you allowed the players, this is where the record sounds.

tracklist.title: The tracks
tracklist.content: The album in order, with lengths. Tap one for the track’s own page.

credits.title: The credits
credits.content: Who played what on the record, and who recorded it.

copies.title: The copies
copies.content: Your own copies of this album — and the ones you have let go of.

more.title: More from them
more.content: Further records by the same artist out of the catalog.

intro.title: The track
intro.content: One track off the album: which record, which place in the running order, how long.

actions.title: What you can do with it
actions.content: Play it, if you allowed the players, and back to the record’s page.

lyrics.title: The words
lyrics.content: If the catalog has them, they are here. If it does not, you can propose them.

credits.title: The credits
credits.content: Who wrote, who played and who recorded this one track.

neighbours.title: Before and after
neighbours.content: The track before and the track after, so the running order can be read through.

intro.title: The pressing
intro.content: One particular release: the same album, but this pressing — with its own year, label and format.

facts.title: What this pressing is
facts.content: Label, catalog number, country, year, format. Enough to tell a record apart in a shop.

tracks.title: The tracks
tracks.content: This pressing’s running order — which is not always the original’s.

intro.title: The label
intro.content: The record company’s page: when it was founded, where, and what in the catalog carries it.

facts.title: What the label is
facts.content: Founding, home, and whatever else the catalog knows about it.

catalog.title: What came out on it
catalog.content: The pressings this company put out — the records open from here.

intro.title: The musician
intro.content: A person rather than a band: what they play, when they were born, and where they have been.

stats.title: The figures
stats.content: How many bands they played in, how many records they are on, and how far their run reaches.

bands.title: Their bands
bands.content: Which band, from when to when, in what role. This is the backbone of the network.

guest.title: Guest appearances
guest.content: Records they played on without ever being a member.

albums.title: Their records
albums.content: Every album they are on, as a member or as a guest.

bandmates.title: Who they played with
bandmates.content: The musicians they shared a band with. The network carries on from here.
